procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - Jaundice
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Wife called yesterday for a same-day slot; they had canceled the March visit because he 'felt run down'. Seen first thing.
Three months of steadily increasing fatigue. Has lost about 10 kg - scale today confirms, 76 kg vs 86 in December. Urine dark like tea for a few weeks; over the past week his wife noticed his eyes and then his skin turning yellow. He denies abdominal pain. No fever, no vomiting, no new meds, no alcohol beyond his usual rare drink.
Exam: thin compared with his baseline, clearly icteric sclerae and jaundiced skin. Afebrile. Abdomen soft, nontender; a smooth rounded fullness under the right costal margin. No ascites. No asterixis.
A: Painless jaundice with weight loss in a 71 y/o - obstructive process until proven otherwise; pancreatic or biliary malignancy high on the list. Family history of pancreatic cancer (paternal uncle).
P: Called GI directly - they will see him Friday 4/21 with labs and ultrasound the same day. Discussed honestly with him and his wife what we are looking for. Return precautions for fever, pain, confusion. I'll call after GI.

reports.text: Indication: jaundice. Liver normal in size and echotexture without focal lesion. Intrahepatic biliary ducts dilated. Common bile duct dilated. Gallbladder distended, no gallstones, no wall thickening, no pericholecystic fluid. Pancreatic head partially obscured by bowel gas. Kidneys normal in size without hydronephrosis. Spleen normal. No ascites.
reports.conclusion: Intra- and extrahepatic biliary dilation without gallstones; distended gallbladder. Cross-sectional imaging recommended.

documents.title: Gastroenterology Consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY - CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 04/21/2023
Urgent referral from primary care.

HPI: 71-year-old man with mild cognitive impairment and left hip osteoarthritis presenting with new symptoms: progressive fatigue for three months, a 10 kg weight loss and dark urine. No abdominal pain. He and his wife have noticed yellowing of his skin and eyes.
PMH: hypertension (lisinopril), type 2 diabetes (metformin), CKD 3a, remote peptic ulcer disease, MCI. PSH: appendectomy.
Medications: lisinopril 10 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg BID, omeprazole 20 mg daily, donepezil 10 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, acetaminophen 500 mg PRN.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: paternal uncle with pancreatic adenocarcinoma; father MI at 71; mother diabetes and stroke at 76.
Social: former smoker (20 pack-years, quit 18 years ago), rare alcohol, retired physics professor.

Exam: Cachectic and jaundiced. Abdomen soft, nontender; the gallbladder is palpable and distended.

Labs today: total bilirubin 5.2 mg/dL (0.3-1.2), direct bilirubin 3.8 mg/dL (0.0-0.3), alkaline phosphatase 420 U/L (40-130), AST 80 U/L (10-40), ALT 75 U/L (7-56).
Abdominal ultrasound today: dilated intra- and extrahepatic bile ducts, no gallstones.

Impression: Painless obstructive jaundice with a Courvoisier gallbladder and weight loss; malignant distal biliary obstruction suspected.
Plan: CT abdomen with pancreatic protocol Monday. If a mass is confirmed, ERCP with biliary stent and EUS-guided tissue sampling next week. Will keep primary care informed.
Outside gastroenterology

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: Indication: obstructive jaundice. Technique: pancreatic protocol, arterial and portal venous phases. Findings: Hypoattenuating mass in the pancreatic head measuring 2.7 x 2.4 cm in axial dimensions. Upstream pancreatic duct mildly dilated. Intra- and extrahepatic bile ducts dilated to the level of the pancreatic head; distended gallbladder without stones. Fat planes about the superior mesenteric artery, celiac axis and portal-superior mesenteric vein confluence preserved. Liver without focal lesion. No ascites. No enlarged lymph nodes. Adrenals, kidneys and spleen unremarkable. Lung bases clear. Colon and small bowel unremarkable. Healed appendectomy.
reports.conclusion: Pancreatic head mass with biliary and pancreatic ductal dilation, no vascular involvement and no evidence of metastatic disease. Findings suspicious for pancreatic adenocarcinoma; tissue sampling recommended.

documents.title: Call with patient and wife - CT result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Spoke with GI this afternoon, then called Mr. and Mrs. Gallo together on speaker. CT shows a mass in the head of the pancreas blocking the bile duct; nothing seen elsewhere, blood vessels look clear. GI is arranging ERCP with a stent and a biopsy for next week. They were quiet but asked good questions. Daughter will drive them. Visit with me booked after the biopsy.

events.reason: ERCP and EUS for pancreatic head mass

conditions.label: Disseminated intravascular coagulation
conditions.note: chronic, low-grade, with the pancreatic adenocarcinoma

reports.text: Specimen: pancreatic head mass, EUS-guided fine-needle biopsy. Microscopic: infiltrating malignant glands with abundant intracellular and extracellular mucin in a desmoplastic stroma. Immunostains support pancreatobiliary origin.
reports.conclusion: Pancreas, head, EUS-guided biopsy: adenocarcinoma, mucin-producing.

documents.title: ERCP and EUS report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY - PROCEDURE REPORT
Date of procedure: 05/02/2023
Procedures: endoscopic ultrasound with fine-needle biopsy; ERCP with biliary stent placement.
Sedation: monitored anesthesia care.
EUS: 2.6 cm hypoechoic mass in the pancreatic head abutting the distal common bile duct; no vascular invasion; no suspicious nodes seen. Three passes with a 22-gauge biopsy needle; on-site evaluation adequate.
ERCP: distal common bile duct stricture; biliary sphincterotomy and placement of a 10 Fr plastic biliary stent with good drainage of bile.
Pre-procedure coagulation: platelets 112 K/uL, PT 15.1 s, INR 1.3, fibrinogen 138 mg/dL, D-dimer 4.6 mcg/mL FEU. No bleeding with sphincterotomy.
Complications: none.
Pathology (05/05): adenocarcinoma, mucin-producing.
Impression: Mucin-producing pancreatic adenocarcinoma of the head, locally resectable by imaging, with laboratory evidence of chronic low-grade disseminated intravascular coagulation.
Plan: referral to surgical oncology placed. Primary care notified.
Allergies: NKDA.
Outside gastroenterology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - Diagnosis Discussion
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
With wife and daughter. ERCP/EUS 5/2: stent placed, biopsy shows mucin-producing adenocarcinoma of the pancreatic head. Clotting tests before the procedure showed low platelets and fibrinogen with a high D-dimer - a low-grade DIC picture that GI attributes to the tumor; no bleeding or clots clinically.
Since the stent: itching gone, urine lighter, eating a bit better. Eyes still faintly yellow.
He understands the diagnosis and wants to hear what surgery can offer. Surgical oncology appointment 5/16.
Exam: less icteric than three weeks ago. Abdomen soft. No bruising or petechiae.
ACP (30 min): health care proxy remains his wife, daughter as alternate. He would want surgery and treatment aimed at cure if offered. Would not want prolonged life support if there were no reasonable hope of recovery. MOLST not completed today; revisit after the surgical plan is known.
Diabetes: A1c last fall in range; continue metformin, may need changes after surgery.
Plan: support, keep me updated; I will coordinate with oncology.

documents.title: Surgical Oncology Consultation
documents.author: surgical oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE SURGICAL ONCOLOGY - CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 05/16/2023

71-year-old man with a 2.6-2.7 cm mucin-producing adenocarcinoma of the pancreatic head presenting with painless jaundice, now stented. Coagulation studies at diagnosis consistent with chronic low-grade DIC, no bleeding or thrombosis.
Comorbidities: hypertension, type 2 diabetes on metformin, CKD 3a, mild cognitive impairment on donepezil, remote PUD. Good functional status, walks daily. NKDA.
CA 19-9 today 210 U/mL (with bilirubin falling after stenting).
Imaging reviewed at tumor board: no arterial or venous involvement, no distant disease - resectable.

Recommendation: pancreaticoduodenectomy, followed by adjuvant chemotherapy with medical oncology. Risks including leak, delayed gastric emptying, infection, bleeding, worsening diabetes and death discussed with patient, wife and daughter; they wish to proceed. Surgery scheduled 06/07/2023. Preoperative evaluation and anesthesia review arranged.
Outside surgical oncology

reports.text: Specimen: pancreaticoduodenectomy (head of pancreas, duodenum, distal bile duct, gallbladder) with regional lymph nodes; plastic biliary stent present. Tumor: invasive adenocarcinoma, mucin-producing, centered in the pancreatic head, 2.8 cm in greatest dimension. Margins: pancreatic neck, bile duct, uncinate/retroperitoneal and enteric margins negative. Lymph nodes: 0 of 16 involved. Gallbladder: no pathologic abnormality.
reports.conclusion: Mucin-producing adenocarcinoma of the pancreatic head, 2.8 cm, margins negative, 0/16 nodes; pT2 N0.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Pancreaticoduodenectomy
documents.author: surgical oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 06/07/2023, discharged 06/16/2023.
Principal diagnosis: mucin-producing adenocarcinoma of the pancreatic head.
Procedure 06/07: open pancreaticoduodenectomy; biliary stent removed with the specimen.
Pathology: 2.8 cm mucin-producing adenocarcinoma, all margins negative, 0 of 16 lymph nodes, pT2 N0.
Course: uncomplicated recovery. Drains removed before discharge. Diet advanced slowly. Insulin sliding scale in hospital; metformin resumed when eating. Coagulation studies trended toward normal after resection; no bleeding.
Discharge medications: lisinopril 10 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, omeprazole 20 mg daily, donepezil 10 mg nightly, aspirin 81 mg daily (resumed on day 5), atorvastatin 40 mg daily, acetaminophen 500 mg as needed.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: surgical clinic in 2 weeks; medical oncology to discuss adjuvant chemotherapy; primary care within 2 weeks.
Outside hospital

documents.title: Post-hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
11 days out from pancreaticoduodenectomy (discharged 6/16). Discharge summary not yet received; history from patient, wife and the discharge paperwork they brought. Path per surgeon's phone call to them: margins clear, nodes negative.
Eating small meals, some early fullness, stools formed. Incision healing. Walking the hallway at home twice a day. No fever. Pain controlled with acetaminophen.
Sugars at home 120s-160s on metformin.
Exam: thin, no jaundice. Incision clean, dry, intact. Abdomen soft. Lungs clear.
Plan: CMP/CBC today. Med list reconciled - unchanged from before surgery. Oncology appointment 7/11 for adjuvant therapy. Call with fever, wound drainage, vomiting.

documents.title: Medical Oncology Consultation
documents.author: medical oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE MEDICAL ONCOLOGY - CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 07/11/2023

Resected pT2 N0 mucin-producing adenocarcinoma of the pancreatic head (pancreaticoduodenectomy 06/07/2023, R0, 0/16 nodes). Recovering well. Comorbid mild cognitive impairment, diabetes, CKD 3a.
Given age, kidney function and cognition, we recommend adjuvant gemcitabine monotherapy, six cycles (days 1, 8, 15 every 28 days), first cycle today. Antiemetics per protocol through our infusion center. Weekly CBC with each dose. Surveillance CT with CA 19-9 after completion and then about every six months.
Allergies: NKDA.
Outside medical oncology

documents.title: Medical Oncology Progress Letter
documents.author: medical oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE MEDICAL ONCOLOGY - PROGRESS NOTE
Date of visit: 08/22/2023
Cycle 3 of adjuvant gemcitabine. Fatigue on the days after infusion, mild nausea controlled with antiemetics; blood counts adequate for each dose.
Labs: platelets 241 K/uL, INR 1.1, fibrinogen 296 mg/dL, D-dimer 0.42 mcg/mL FEU - the coagulation abnormalities seen at diagnosis have resolved after resection. CA 19-9 31 U/mL.
Plan: continue gemcitabine to complete six cycles in January.
Outside medical oncology

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV during adjuvant chemo (cycle 4). Oncology OK'd vaccines today, between infusion weeks.
Oncology letter 8/22: coagulation numbers back to normal after surgery, CA 19-9 31 - DIC off the active list.
Tired on infusion weeks, otherwise walking daily. Weight holding near 72-73. PHQ-2 1. Memory per wife unchanged; donepezil continues. Not driving.
No falls. Uses a cane on bad hip days.
Exam: vitals as charted. Healed upper abdominal incision. Lungs clear.
Plan: labs; high-dose flu, RSV and updated COVID today. Return November.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
September A1c 7.0, up from his usual mid-6s - expected after losing part of the pancreas. Kidney function at baseline. Fasting home sugars 130s.
One cycle of gemcitabine left. Appetite fair.
Exam: BP fine, weight stable.
Plan: same metformin dose for now; at his age and stage A1c around 7 is a reasonable target. Recheck early next year.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: Indication: surveillance after pancreaticoduodenectomy for pancreatic adenocarcinoma. Postsurgical changes of pancreaticoduodenectomy with intact pancreaticojejunostomy, hepaticojejunostomy and gastrojejunostomy. No soft tissue at the surgical bed. Mild pneumobilia, expected. Liver without focal lesion. No ascites, no adenopathy. Kidneys, adrenals, spleen unremarkable. Lung bases clear.
reports.conclusion: Expected postoperative changes. No evidence of recurrent or metastatic disease.

documents.title: Medical Oncology Follow-up
documents.author: medical oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE MEDICAL ONCOLOGY - FOLLOW-UP
Date of visit: 01/30/2024
Completed six cycles of adjuvant gemcitabine on 01/09/2024. Energy improving.
Surveillance CT 01/23/2024: postsurgical changes, no evidence of recurrence. CA 19-9 24 U/mL.
Plan: surveillance CT and CA 19-9 about every six months for the first years. Return August.
Outside medical oncology

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Chemo finished in January; oncology CT clear, CA 19-9 24. Regaining weight - up 2 kg. Appetite good.
No chest pain, no breathlessness, no swelling. Home BP mostly 130s.
Exam: BP acceptable. Lungs clear, no edema.
Plan: CMP, CBC, A1c. Continue meds. AWV in September.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yesterday's labs: blood count normal, liver tests normal, kidney function at your baseline, A1c 7.0 - about where it has settled since the surgery. No changes.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT - PHYSICIAN RECORD
Date of service: 04/29/2024

CC: sudden severe shortness of breath.
HPI: 72-year-old man with resected pancreatic adenocarcinoma (2023), hypertension, type 2 diabetes and CKD stage 3a, brought in by ambulance after abrupt onset of severe dyspnea while watching television this evening, with a cough bringing up pink, frothy sputum.
Meds (per patient list): lisinopril 10 mg, metformin 1000 mg BID, omeprazole 20 mg, donepezil 10 mg, aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, acetaminophen PRN.
Allergies: NKDA.

Triage vitals: RR 30, BP 180/100, HR 110, SpO2 85% on room air.
Exam: tachypneic, speaking in short phrases. Rales bilaterally to the mid-lung fields. JVP elevated. S3 gallop. No leg edema.
ABG on room air: pH 7.32, PaCO2 50 mmHg, PaO2 58 mmHg, HCO3 24 mEq/L.
NT-proBNP 2840 pg/mL. hs-troponin I 18 ng/L.
CXR: pulmonary venous congestion with septal lines.
ECG: sinus tachycardia, no acute ST changes.

ED course: BiPAP, high-dose nitroglycerin, IV furosemide 40 mg. Marked improvement within the first hour, SpO2 95% on BiPAP then 93% on 2 L.
Impression: flash pulmonary edema in the setting of severe hypertension.
Disposition: admitted to telemetry/medicine for further management and echocardiogram.
Regional hospital emergency department

documents.title: Wife reports hospitalization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Wife called. He was taken by ambulance a week ago Monday with sudden trouble breathing - 'fluid on the lungs' - admitted three nights, home Thursday 5/2. Doing well at home, breathing normal, sleeping flat. They gave him a new water pill. ED note came to us 5/3; no discharge summary yet. Post-hospital visit booked 5/9; asked her to bring all bottles and the discharge papers.

documents.title: Fill history review
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Ran external fill history ahead of Thursday's visit: furosemide 20 mg tabs #30, one daily, filled 05/02/2024 at a community pharmacy, prescribed by the hospital discharging physician. No other new fills. Added to med list as an outside prescription pending review.

orders.order: Records request: hospital discharge summary and echocardiogram, 04/2024 admission

documents.title: Post-hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen with wife after admission 4/29-5/2 for flash pulmonary edema. ED record reviewed: BP 180/100, SpO2 85% RA, rales to mid-lungs, S3, ABG 7.32/50/58, NT-proBNP 2840, troponin 18; BiPAP, nitro, IV furosemide. No discharge summary yet.
Per patient and wife: they 'did an ultrasound of the heart and said the pumping was normal'. Sent home on furosemide 20 mg daily (confirmed by bottle and fill history). No other changes.
Now: no dyspnea walking around the block, no orthopnea, no PND, no leg swelling. Home BP 128-140/70s since discharge.
Exam: vitals as charted. JVP not elevated. Lungs clear. Heart regular, no gallop today. No edema.
A/P
1. Flash pulmonary edema, hypertensive - recovered. Continue lisinopril 10 and furosemide 20 as discharged. BMP today on the new diuretic.
2. Requesting discharge summary and echo report.
3. Other problems unchanged.
Return precautions reviewed. Recheck in 6-8 weeks.

documents.title: Records request follow-up
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hospital discharge summary and echo from the April admission still not here. Called the hospital release-of-information line; they show the request as received. Resent request by fax. Will flag for PCP if nothing by July.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Two months after the pulmonary edema admission. No recurrence of breathlessness. Taking furosemide each morning. May BMP: potassium and creatinine at his baseline.
Hospital records still outstanding despite two requests; we'll work with what we have.
Exam: BP at goal. Lungs clear. No edema.
Plan: BMP, A1c. Continue current regimen. Oncology surveillance due in August.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: Comparison 01/23/2024. Stable postsurgical changes after pancreaticoduodenectomy. No soft tissue mass at the surgical bed. No new liver lesion. No ascites or adenopathy. Lung bases clear.
reports.conclusion: No evidence of recurrent or metastatic disease.

documents.title: Medical Oncology Surveillance
documents.author: medical oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE MEDICAL ONCOLOGY - SURVEILLANCE VISIT
Date of visit: 08/20/2024
Seven months after completing adjuvant gemcitabine for resected pT2 N0 pancreatic adenocarcinoma. Interval admission in April for flash pulmonary edema, recovered.
CT 08/13/2024: no evidence of recurrence. CA 19-9 within normal limits.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV with wife and daughter.
Oncology August: CT clear. No breathing trouble since April.
Function: ADLs independent, needs prompting for some tasks per wife; IADLs mostly by wife. Does not drive. Cane outdoors for the hip. No falls. PHQ-2 0.
Cognition: wife feels memory is slowly worse but he still reads daily and follows the news closely. Donepezil continues. Neurology follow-up lapsed during the cancer year - they would like to reconnect; I gave them the office number.
Eye exam: due, they will book.
Exam: vitals as charted. Lungs clear, heart regular, no edema. Feet intact.
Plan: labs; high-dose flu and updated COVID today. RSV done last year. Continue meds.

conditions.label: ST elevation myocardial infarction of anterior wall
conditions.note: proximal LAD, treated with DES; course complicated by myocardial reperfusion injury

medications.drug: 24 HR metoprolol succinate 25 MG Extended Release Oral Tablet

reports.text: Sinus rhythm. ST-segment elevation in V1 through V3. No other acute changes.
reports.conclusion: Anterior ST elevation, consistent with acute anterior STEMI.

reports.text: Left ventricle normal in size. LVEF approximately 50% by biplane method. Mild hypokinesis of the anteroseptal wall. Normal right ventricular size and function. No significant valvular disease. No pericardial effusion.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Anterior STEMI
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - CARDIOLOGY DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 10/17/2024 via the emergency department; discharged 10/20/2024.

Presentation: 73-year-old man, six months after an admission for flash pulmonary edema, brought in with crushing chest pain radiating to the left shoulder. ECG: ST elevation V1-V3. STEMI alert activated.
Catheterization 10/17: acute occlusion of the proximal left anterior descending artery, treated with a single drug-eluting stent with TIMI 3 flow restored. Other vessels without flow-limiting disease. Right radial access.
CK-MB before PCI 9.4 ng/mL, rising to 81 ng/mL after reperfusion; interpreted as myocardial reperfusion injury. No arrhythmia on telemetry.
Echo 10/18: LVEF about 50%, mild anteroseptal hypokinesis.
Diagnoses: acute anterior STEMI treated with PCI/DES to the proximal LAD; myocardial reperfusion injury.
Other history: resected pancreatic adenocarcinoma (2023, mucin-producing, with chronic DIC at diagnosis), hypertension, type 2 diabetes, CKD 3a, mild cognitive impairment, hip osteoarthritis, remote PUD.
Discharge medications: aspirin 81 mg daily; clopidogrel 75 mg daily for 12 months - do not stop without cardiology; metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily (new); atorvastatin 40 mg daily; lisinopril 10 mg daily; metformin 1000 mg BID; omeprazole 20 mg daily; donepezil 10 mg nightly; acetaminophen PRN; furosemide 20 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: cardiology in 6 weeks; primary care within 1 week.
Regional hospital cardiology

documents.title: Daughter reports heart attack
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Daughter called. Dad had a heart attack Thursday, stent placed the same morning, home Sunday. Two new pills. Doing okay, a little tired. Post-hospital visit 10/24 with PCP; she'll bring the discharge packet. Reviewed chest pain precautions - call 911.

documents.title: Post-hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
With daughter. Admitted 10/17-10/20 for anterior STEMI: per the discharge instructions sheet, proximal LAD stent same morning. Formal discharge summary not yet received.
Meds reconciled from the packet: NEW clopidogrel 75 daily (12 months, per cardiology) and metoprolol succinate 25 daily. Continuing aspirin 81, atorvastatin 40, lisinopril 10, furosemide 20, metformin, omeprazole, donepezil, acetaminophen PRN.
No chest pain since. Mild fatigue. Radial site healed. No bleeding or dark stools.
Exam: BP and HR as charted (pulse slower on metoprolol). R wrist without hematoma. Lungs clear. Heart regular, no murmur. No edema.
A/P: Anterior STEMI s/p DES. Dual antiplatelet - omeprazole already on board, good given ulcer history. Labs today. Cardiology follow-up early December. Return precautions. See me again in January.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Blood count and kidney panel from yesterday are fine on the new heart medicines. No bleeding signal. Keep the cardiology appointment in December.

documents.title: Cardiology Follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE CARDIOLOGY - OFFICE NOTE
Date of visit: 12/05/2024
Seven weeks after anterior STEMI with proximal LAD drug-eluting stent (10/17/2024); echo LVEF about 50% with mild anteroseptal hypokinesis. No angina since discharge, walking daily with his wife, no dyspnea, no bleeding.
Exam: BP and heart rate controlled. Lungs clear. No edema.
Plan: continue aspirin 81 mg and clopidogrel 75 mg to complete 12 months (through 10/2025), metoprolol succinate 25 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, lisinopril 10 mg, furosemide 20 mg. Return in 10 months.
Outside cardiology
